commits.message:
Single-source the classifier's replay requirements and gate on the predecessor ledger

The header classifier carried three literal category lists: the families
whose fault proof opens prev_utxos_root and therefore need the
authenticated predecessor ledger, and (twice) the families whose
detection replays the historical native-script corpus. The watcher
kept its own copy of the first list and gated fault decisions on
`replayContext === undefined`. That gate was vacuous in production:
the launch scope always includes crossBlockDuplicateEvent, whose
settlement capture attaches a context to every decision, so a
predecessor-family decision that omitted the predecessor passed.

Both sets now live in workflow/replay-requirements.ts as
PREDECESSOR_LEDGER_PROOF_CATEGORIES and
HISTORICAL_CORPUS_REPLAY_CATEGORIES with a `launchScopeRequires`
helper; the classifier and the watcher derive from them. The doc
comments record that these are not the registry's `requires` sets:
`replayContext` there means the artifact re-derives from the admitted
context object, which is a different fact enforced at load time.

The watcher's decision-time gate now checks the invariant the
classifier actually establishes: a fault decision in a predecessor
family on a header that commits a non-empty previous ledger must carry
`replayContext.predecessor`. A genesis-ledger header is admitted
without one. Families that only need the context object are admitted
at decision time and refused by their application record at load,
which the tests pin per family. Disabling the gate fails exactly the
eight refusal cases.

New tests pin both sets against the catalogue and the registry: the
corpus set is a strict subset of the historicalNativeScriptAuthority
families, and the ledger set intersects the registry's replayContext
families in exactly noReferenceInput and nonExistentInput.

Closes #677.

Speed up the watcher and fault-proof test suites

The fault-proof suite drops from about 43 to about 20 minutes at eight
forks and the watcher suite from about 26 minutes at two forks to about
four at eight, with every test still isolated per file. The savings come
from removing repeated work rather than from adding forks:

- core validation-merkle: memoize the membership index per leaf array so
  proofs for a 1,304-asset value no longer rebuild the frontier per leaf.
- sdk blueprint: apply blueprint parameters with the aiken uplc wasm
  applier (byte-identical to the JavaScript applier over every
  parameterised validator, roughly ten times faster) and key the applied
  script cache by the raw inputs instead of hashing the compiled code on
  every lookup. Adds @lucid-evolution/uplc as a direct sdk dependency at
  the pin lucid already uses.
- fault-proofs journal: fold the workflow incrementally instead of
  revalidating the whole journal on every append and load.
- fault-proofs runtime: memoize the seed-derived signer per Lucid
  instance instead of re-deriving the BIP32 key on every step.
- mint-authorization: index the batch generator by encoded state instead
  of replaying from the first batch on every evaluate step, and memoize
  artifact admission by digest.
- transition-trace: memoize the MPF trie per root object.
- watcher catalogue fixture: emit definite-length CBOR for positional
  script bytes; the indefinite heads made cbor-x decode pathologically.
- watcher user-event-history test: compare byte stores by content rather
  than through deep equality on large typed arrays.
- watcher vitest: derive the fork count from the host with an override
  through MIDGARD_WATCHER_FORKS.
- fault-proofs vitest: rank the longest emulator files first on cold
  runs, record the measured suite shape, and pick the evaluator per
  harness. Scalus stays the default for mint authorization because two
  size-at-maximum cases pass under it while the aiken evaluator reports
  them a few thousand memory units over the limit; that disagreement is
  an open question and is documented at the harness option. Lifecycles
  away from the limit opt into the faster aiken evaluator.

Document that the retained-DA transport starts locally and is not retried in process

The shared retained-DA transport does not dial a peer when it starts: it
builds the local libp2p node with inbound gated and no listen address, and
peers are dialed per retrieval request under a lease. A start failure is
therefore local and deterministic. The classification that first needs the
transport fails closed, the process exits 70 with the error in its
failed_closed record, and a restart owns a fresh transport, so the sticky
failed status needs no in-process retry with backoff.

Say so in the owner's status comment, the README readiness section, and the
challenger runbook, and name the two tests after the start failure they
exercise instead of a dial.

Test the watcher's decision-time predecessor-authority gate per family

The gate in the fault-proof application's classifyHeader entry refuses a
fault decision for a family whose record requires the predecessor replay
context when the classifier retained none. Until now only the set was
pinned; the check itself, its refusal, and what the runner later sees were
untested for the three families #675 widened it to. The new table-driven
test drives the real entry with the classifier module as a double: every
predecessor family is refused at the exact message and leaves no replay
context for its runner, whose record then refuses at its own requires
gate; every predecessor family with a retained context is admitted and the
loader hands that context to the record, which resolves exactly its
roster; every other installed family is admitted without one. Disabling
the gate fails exactly the five refusal cases.

Report the shared retained-DA transport in operations status

Startup readiness stopped opening the retained-DA transport in #675, so
its health needs a live home. The retained-DA runtime owner now exposes
the state of its one shared transport (idle until the first workflow
launch, opening, open, failed with the dial error, closed); the fault-proof
application delegates to it and operations status carries it, adding the
retained_da_transport_failed readiness reason when a dial has failed.
Closing an owner whose dial failed no longer re-throws the dial error.
The watcher README states what startup readiness proves versus what
operations status reports.

Re-measure the transition-trace workflow fit ledger against the current blueprint

The committed ledger was bound to blueprint 11593a4e; the installed
lifecycle test re-derives it from the blueprint in use and has rewritten it
in every session since. Same 486 entries, re-measured against 04790ae6
under the same compiler.

Add the authenticated event-history architecture proposal for NIFP-01 to 03

A design document proposing a cumulative authenticated event dictionary
with deterministic shards and immutable checkpoints, its security
properties, alternatives, retention, batched-admission fallback, cost
model and acceptance criteria, plus a research note recording the current
fabricated-event, watcher retention and transition-trace boundaries it
starts from. Status is Proposed; remaining-gaps.md now points at it and
records that the gaps stay open until it is accepted and implemented.

Drop the prose facts and voice checks and enforce lint and format in CI

The docs-site facts check restated source inventories in a script and the
voice check pattern-matched wording; both went red on ordinary source drift
without proving a documentation claim, and their trigger lists had to
mirror every source they read. They are removed with their CI steps and
path triggers; the link check stays. The documentation policy and the
catalogue-status table now say plainly that prose counts are verified by
reading the source. The demo workspace lint and format-check that the
pre-commit hook applies locally are now enforced in midgard-node-ci.yml,
which the hook's header cites instead of the retired gate names. The cg1
control-publication gate no longer verifies the exclusion's prose citation
against the necessity memo; the exclusion itself is still checked for
genuine absence and for being a real role.

Verify the family registry program against its baseline and review the glossary (#676)

Full fault-proofs and watcher suites re-run once against a fresh blueprint
(byte-identical to the one on disk) and reconciled with the ticket-1
baseline; the watcher journey suite and node-tools typecheck are green.
The glossary entries for the family application registry and the family
record are reviewed against the landed code: the allow-list is gone, the
registry's key set is the installed set, a record carries the
decision-digest flag and refuses a missing required part unless a
reconciliation-only permit is held, and hand-written rows declare their
type arguments.

Derive the watcher's installed set from the registry and take secrets off readiness (#675)

The watcher application no longer names a family. Its installed set is the
family application registry's keys read in the SDK catalogue's presentation
order, so every launch-scope comparison (classifier, supervisor, decision
bridge, journal) still sees the one order it compared against before; the
missing set is the catalogue's complement of the registry and stays empty.
The decision-time predecessor check reads the records' `requires` through
`WATCHER_PREDECESSOR_AUTHORITY_CATEGORIES`, widening the refusal from the
two hand-listed families to the five that require the replay context at load
time, as #668 asks, so the two lists can no longer disagree.

Startup readiness now runs on a readiness-only path. The shared loader body
is split into `bindWatcherDeploymentAuthority` (local-node authority,
manifest/blueprint/deployment info, manifest-vs-config finality, Lucid and
the roster resolver; no secret) and the acting `buildCommonInfrastructure`
on top of it (prover wallet, node admin key, signer, lease coordinator,
optional parts). Readiness admits its runtime configuration through the new
`readAdmittedWatcherRuntimeConfig`, shared with the workflow loader so both
refuse a non-canonical path or a foreign deployment in the same words, and
then only resolves the family's roster. It therefore reads neither secret,
opens no retained-DA transport and acquires no lease; the prover wallet and
admin key are proven present by the trusted-head startup phase. A closed
application refuses readiness through the same admitted-set the other
methods already consult.

Tests follow #668's third seam: readiness lists exactly the registry roster
and reads no secret (file-backed key sources whose read would throw); the
acting loader still fails closed on a missing secret; a family whose record
requires the replay context the classifier never captured refuses through
the watcher-built infrastructure with the shared error, for all five such
families, before the resolver is asked for anything, while a family requiring
only what the watcher always supplies is applied against exactly its roster.
The test-only application exposes its runtime loader for that purpose
(`unsafeExposeRuntimeLoaderForTest`, refused for an executing application),
because exercising an installed runner needs a classifier-issued actuation
permit for each family. No live `runOrResume` test covers the three newly
refused families at decision time; that needs a classifier fixture per
family and is left to the integrated verification in #676.

Docs name the registry as the installed-category source (watcher README,
catalogue-status, offchain-reference, the dispute workflow page), and the
dispute page no longer claims readiness asserts move-completeness.

Move the workflow loader boundary up to common infrastructure

The compiled runtime loader used to hand each family runner an
already-bound family config, so every host had to know how to lay out
55 config shapes: the watcher carried a tagged config union, a
57-overload layout function, a tag-unwrapping loader per family, a
constructor switch, an out-ref flattener and a hand-written runner
table, and the runtime had to erase the loader's config to `unknown`
at the host boundary.

The loader now returns the one shape every family draws from: the
common infrastructure, the reference-script resolver, the public
retained-DA transports and a disposer. The generic run-or-resume body
applies the family application record itself (resolve the roster, bind
the config, construct, assert the identity), so a family is applied to
an invocation in exactly one place and no caller ever names a family's
config. The body refuses loaded infrastructure whose header or decision
digest differs from the invocation, exempts missing required parts only
under reconciliation-only authority, and still demands the adapter
recovery surface before resuming a recorded workflow.

The watcher builds common infrastructure once, implements the
validation-challenge port over its capture map, installs the registry's
runner factories in a loop, and reports startup readiness by resolving
the registry roster without constructing a workflow. The
`constructWorkflow` dependency seam and the per-family loader surfaces
are deleted (6,114 -> ~1,700 lines). Readiness out-refs are keyed by
roster role, as the registry defines them; the watcher application test
now derives the expected roster from the registry instead of a
transcription.

Enforcing the records' requirements at load time exposed that the
valueNotPreserved record demanded the predecessor replay context, which
the watcher had only ever bound optionally and which the workflow proves
without: the record now binds the context when the host supplies it and
requires nothing, keeping the replay-context requirement on the five
families the spec names.

Refs #668 #674 #675

Derive the runner factory table from the family application registry (#674)

WORKFLOW_RUNNER_FACTORIES is now one map over FAMILY_APPLICATION_REGISTRY
through the module-private admission and the generic run-or-resume body.
The linear-definition derivation loop, the explicit doubleSpend constructor
and the 36 explicit record rows are gone: registering a record is what adds
a family's row. The registry's RegisteredFamilyCategory /
REGISTERED_FAMILY_CATEGORIES aliases, pure copies of the catalogue since
#673, are deleted with them.

The table's factories take the runtime loader at `unknown`: the registry
states every record at one erased shape, so the table cannot relate a
host's loaded config to the family's config type. The watcher's per-family
loaders (the one live caller) previously had that check at compile time and
now meet it at runtime in constructWorkflow; #675 replaces those loaders
with the records' own bindConfig, which restores the pairing by
construction. Flagged on the ticket as an owner call.

Refusal behaviour of the generic body is tested once, one test per check
(category mismatch, missing disposer, unsupported schema, non-public DA
source, identity mismatch, digest mismatch when flagged), plus one
table-wide test that every row exposes only the shared drive surface and
one that every row refuses a foreign category naming its own. The eleven
per-surface copies in family test files are deleted; their non-runner
assertions stay. Consumers of the deleted doubleSpend constructor (three
fault-proofs tests, the watcher application and two watcher tests) use the
table row.

Gates: fault-proofs typecheck + lint green; 18 focused fault-proofs files
588 tests green; watcher, node and node-tools typecheck green; watcher
funding/retained-DA tests green. Full fault-proofs suite running in the
background per the 2026-09-21 owner rule.

Register the four bespoke families and empty the allow-list (#673)

Hand-written records for missingSignature, networkId, valueNotPreserved
and validationTraceDispute complete the family application registry:
every one of the 55 catalogue categories now has a record, the
NOT_YET_REGISTERED_FAMILY_CATEGORIES allow-list is gone, and the registry
is typed as one mapped row per catalogue category (an explicit erased
FamilyApplicationRegistryEntry annotation: with all 55 rows present tsc
can no longer serialize the inferred type, TS7056).

validationTraceDispute is the only record with requires.validationChallenge.
Its bindConfig obtains the challenge from the host's port, so the record
contract now allows bindConfig to return Config | Promise<Config> and the
shared loop awaits it. The validation-dispute runner surface is deleted;
its canonical-block currency check moves into
assertValidationTraceDisputeChallengeCurrent, run by the uniform
runOrResumeManifestBoundValidationTraceDisputeWorkflow({workflow, sources,
journal}) entry the record executes. This runs the check inside the
generic runner's execute step, i.e. after the reconciliation-only and
pending-continuation gates rather than before them.

The four explicit runtime constructors and their watcher rows become
record-derived rows through familyApplicationWorkflowRunnerFactory;
adapters cite the records as their existing surface.

Deviation from the ticket text: networkId's roster carries no state-queue
removal set. ManifestBoundNetworkIdWorkflowConfig has no place for one
(its removal field takes only the lease coordinator and validity window;
the adapter resolves the removal scripts from deployment info), and the
watcher's own networkId roster never had one either.

Registry table test generalized over the new shapes (top-level network-id
layout, forced/union/control groups, step-free roster), pinned sets
extended, allow-list assertion replaced by whole-catalogue coverage, a
sentinel challenge port proves the port's answer lands under `challenge`.
Shared-loop test covers refusal without the port and binding with it. The
installed dispute lifecycle test drives executeManifestBound... directly;
a new test covers the currency check in both polarities.

Fault-proofs typecheck: 24.5/24.1 s before this slice, 19.1/19.0 s after
(ticket 1 measured 17.8 s -> 18.8 s). Gates green: fault-proofs typecheck
and lint, registry/loop/runtime/dispute tests, watcher, node and
node-tools typecheck.

Register the twelve no-digest cursor families on their own shapes (#672)

Derive the records of the twelve cursor families whose config carries no
decision digest: the plain nativeScriptInvalid; nativeScriptDecoding,
mintAuthorization and withdrawalMistag, which require the predecessor
replay context; and the eight historical families (minAda,
missingNativeScriptTx, missingNativeScriptUtxo, transitionTrace,
crossBlockDuplicateEvent, resolvedOutputNonCanonical,
spendInputSignerMissing, executionNativeScriptInvalid), which require the
historical native-script authority and lay its history source and
checkpoint store into the config under the field names each family reads.

A record declares the infrastructure it requires beside its roster; the
builders refuse at import a historical flag without a layout or a layout
without the flag, and an auxiliary-script key without a declaration or the
reverse. The shared bundle builder covers nine families, the authenticated
certificate builder now takes requirements for the two certificate-shape
historical families, and transitionTrace lays the derived roster into its
contract-name-keyed map by hand. The allow-list shrinks from sixteen to
four.

The three remaining family-local runner surfaces are deleted along with
the twelve explicit runtime constructors; every row is derived from its
record and the watcher launches through WORKFLOW_RUNNER_FACTORIES. The
execution native-script run takes the uniform {workflow, sources, journal}
input and reads the admitted digest from the journal, which the generic
runner binds from the invocation, so the equality check it replaced holds
by construction.

Table tests cover the twelve with no per-family additions: bound
references are checked as a multiset against the roster whatever the
shape, the digest-binding set and both requirement sets are pinned, and
every record is checked to bind exactly the optional infrastructure it
requires. The shared loop test covers both requirements in both
polarities.

Register the eight decision-digest families on the certificate shape (#671)

Register fieldItemWidthIllegal, fieldPreimageLengthMismatch,
mintItemNonCanonical, outputReferenceScriptDecoding,
protectedOutputSignerMissing, transactionOutputNonCanonical,
witnessScriptDecoding and unusedScriptWitness in the family application
registry, shrinking the not-yet-registered allow-list by eight.

Six records are derived by a new builder for the authenticated certificate
shape: the roster is the definition's chain steps, witness roles and
certificate, and bindConfig lays each step under the config key its
manifest-contracts map names, so fieldPreimageLengthMismatch keeps its
step02Accepted/step02Forced keys without restating them. The builder refuses
a definition without a certificate or with auxiliary reference scripts, and
refuses an invocation without the admitted decision digest. unusedScriptWitness
is derived by the existing removal-set builder, which now shares the same
digest refusal. mintItemNonCanonical has no definition and is the one
hand-written record, laid out on the same certificate shape with its step keys
and witness roles read from its manifest-contracts map. The common
infrastructure fields every bound config copies are now laid in by one shared
helper. Every row names its exact config and workflow types.

fieldPreimageLengthMismatch previously ran on an explicit row that skipped
the decision-digest identity check; its record sets the flag, since its
config and workflow already carry the digest the invocation admits.

The seven family-local runner surfaces and their Loaded/Load types are
deleted; the runtime's runner table derives their rows from the records, and
the watcher launches them through that table. unusedScriptWitness consumes
the shared removal-set constant instead of restating the nine names. The
tests that imported a surface by name are retargeted to the derived runner,
and the registry table tests cover the eight, accepting both the bundle and
the flat certificate shape, without per-family additions.

Deleting the surfaces also drops dead imports from the family modules, which
changes module evaluation order. The transition-trace installed lifecycle
test relied on that order: its module mock of the local L1 observation port
did not reach the transition-trace event authority once the modules
evaluated differently, and the test failed on an empty source. It now
injects the recorder's raw authority through the existing test-only entry
point instead of depending on the mock reaching that caller.
